previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and hemorrhoids, was admitted with chest pain, abdominal pain, and gastrointestinal bleeding. He also reported hematuria and dysuria. Initial evaluation showed no acute cardiac ischemia, with normal troponins and ECGs. The GI bleed was attributed to hemorrhoids, with stable hemoglobin. Liver enzymes were elevated consistent with alcoholic hepatitis, improving during the stay. A urine analysis indicated a urinary tract infection, treated with ciprofloxacin, and a renal ultrasound revealed an enlarged prostate. The patient eloped before a scheduled echocardiogram but returned later to receive discharge instructions and prescriptions. He was discharged home with plans to follow up for cardiac testing, urology evaluation, and continuation of treatment for alcohol-related liver disease and infection.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, continuous

# pancreatitis: Most likely due to alcohol as patient admits 
drinking at least ___ pint of brandy everynight. Could also be 
___ gallstone pancreatitis, however, this is less likely as the 
RUQ US did not show signs of cholestatic duct dilatation. 
Patient was made NPO for bowel rest, was given IVF, IV dilaudid 
for pain, and IV zofran for nausea/vomiting.  After 5 days, he 
was transitioned to low residue/low fat diet, as the patient 
reported that he would not stand for a clear diet.  He tolerated 
the PO diet without vomiting. Patient reports stable abdominal 
pain in the epigastric region throughout hospital course. He was 
also hemodynamically stable throughout hospital course.   

#Productive cough: Patient reported a nonproductive cough in the 
middle of his hospitalization associated with some chest 
tightness.  Patient remained afebrile, lungs CTAB, no WBC, so 
unlikely a pneumonia. He received PRN albuterol inhaler, which 
helped withthe chest tightness.  His cough resolved. 
   
# alcohol abuse: serum alcohol upon arrival 202. His last drink 
was 12hrs prior to admission. He denies history DT. He was 
palced on CIWA protol, but never showed signs of withdrawal and 
never scored on CIWA. He was given a multivitamin, folic acid, 
and thiamine.

# chest pain: Likely ___ alcohol induced gastritis or ___ 
pancreatitis. Less likely ACS due to negative tropTx2 and no EKG 
abnormalities. He underwent ETT-MIBI recently and was 
reassuring, but eloped on last admission prior to scheduled TTE.
